title: C slice: coap_server.c receives POST coap://[ff02::1]/sos (R-12-036)
description: C/Zephyr slice of l1qw.37 item (1); Python sibling landed in l1qw.37.1 (worker7, commit 1502f60252). spec/12-apps.md 18.4 R-12-036: SOS MUST be postable to coap://[ff02::1]/sos. sos_post in lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_server.c:448 is transport-agnostic (Zephyr coap_server dispatches by URI path), so the handler needs NO change — the gap is group membership/delivery. Investigation (worker7): Zephyr joins ff02::1 only via join_mcast_allnodes() (zephyr subsys/net/ip/net_if.c:1135) which exists ONLY under CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MLD (no-op macro otherwise, net_if.c:1218), called from join_mcast_nodes when the L2 sets NET_L2_MULTICAST. LICHEN's L2 DOES set NET_L2_MULTICAST (lichen_l2_init.c:506) and uses standard ND/MLD for all-nodes (comment :494). Work: (a) verify/enable CONFIG_NET_IPV6_MLD in the puck app confs (some tests explicitly set MLD=n: coap_oscore_fallback, ble_ingress); (b) confirm ff02::1-destined CoAP POSTs reach the service socket and sos_post runs (native_sim test or twister); (c) if MLD-on-RF-report traffic is unacceptable on LoRa, add an explicit net_if_mcast_join(iface, ff02::1) at lichen_coap_server_start() behind a Kconfig instead, documenting the tradeoff. LoRa is a true broadcast medium so RX filtering is not the blocker; the stack-level group membership is.
close_reason: C slice complete: MLD pinned in puck conf, membership ztest landed with both variants green on native_sim, reviewer convergence reached. E2E POST proof filed as P3 follow-up.
